_comment: Single source of truth for the Zephyr SDK (cross-toolchain) pin -- a DECLARED, hand-maintained input, the same kind of fact metadata/bootstrap.json is, and living beside it for that reason. This is NOT alp.lock: alp.lock is GENERATED by `west alp-lock` to record what a workspace actually RESOLVED to, and metadata/schemas/alp-lock-v1.schema.json:88-91 already reserves an unpopulated `toolchain` object for that future *resolved/verified* identity -- a different concept from this file's *declared pin*. Leave that key reserved; do not populate it from here, and do not conflate the two: this file is read BEFORE any workspace exists (a fresh CI runner has no resolved anything yet), alp-lock's `toolchain` key would describe what got installed AFTER the fact. scripts/check_toolchain_lock.py is the drift gate: it asserts (1) this file validates against its schema, (2) zephyrSdk.version equals the real `SDK_VERSION` file in the Zephyr revision metadata/bootstrap.json's `zephyr.version` pins -- the exact derivation that makes a value like the historical `SDK_VER=0.16.8` literal in pr-renode-aen-smoke.yml (pinned to no Zephyr revision this repo has ever built against; see the gate's own module docstring for the git-blame finding) impossible to reintroduce unnoticed -- and (3) no CI workflow hardcodes an SDK version or downloads an SDK archive without sourcing both from this file and verifying its sha256 afterward. Read (3) as the scope it is, not as the invariant you want it to be (#1012): the gate scans THIS repo's .github/workflows only, so a consumer in another repo is outside it entirely -- tan-cli's `ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_VERSION` hand-tracks `zephyrSdk.version` to print the exact `west sdk install --version` a customer runs, and is covered only because tan-cli PR #173 vendors this file and asserts byte-parity in its own required test. A NEW consumer of this pin needs its own parity assertion; widening this scan will not reach it. Per docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md's Decision, every artifact below is pinned at upstream's own canonical URL and never rehosted: GPLv3 corresponding-source obligations on the GCC-based toolchains, an unreviewed Arm EULA, and a download domain with zero AV reputation are all costs a rehost would carry that a pin does not. `toolchain_gnu_linux-aarch64_arm-zephyr-eabi.tar.xz` also exists upstream at this SDK release but is deliberately not listed below -- no current alp-sdk path runs a linux-aarch64 CI job or downloads it -- the schema's `host` enum permits recording it later without a schema bump; add the row only once something reads it. Each artifact also carries `tier`/`licence` (issue #1603, follow-on to #1574): ADR 0021 SS3's one-consent-screen facts (artifact/source/size/licence), the two facts metadata/bootstrap.json's `artifactProvenance` (#1574) covers for the 8 package-manager prerequisites but deliberately left OUT of scope for these two hermetic archives, whose `source` (`baseUrl`+`filename`) and `sizeBytes` already lived here. See `measuredFootprint.notes` below for why `licence` is null on every row.

zephyrSdk.versionDerivation: Equal to the `SDK_VERSION` file at the Zephyr revision metadata/bootstrap.json's `zephyr.version` pins (currently v4.4.1) -- verified with `git show <zephyr.version>:SDK_VERSION` against the Zephyr checkout, not copied by hand. scripts/check_toolchain_lock.py re-derives and asserts this at every run.

notes: Measured on a real host, not estimated -- this replaces docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md's Open-evidence item on real per-artifact sizes: that ADR's ~1 GB (minimal SDK + arm-zephyr-eabi) to ~17 GB (full bundle) figures were a comment in pr-twister.yml, never a measurement, and both directions turn out wrong here.
Compressed download, linux-x86_64 minimal-sdk + arm-zephyr-eabi-toolchain: 70650944 + 101752776 = 172403720 bytes (~164 MiB) -- the ADR's ~1 GB estimate for the same pair was ~6x too high.

Extracted on disk for that same minimal + arm-zephyr-eabi install (du -sb): whole SDK 2026739200 bytes (~1.89 GiB); hosttools/ 1242632545 bytes (~1.16 GiB); gnu/arm-zephyr-eabi/ 784086497 bytes (~748 MiB).

Design consequence: hosttools/ is 61% of the on-disk footprint -- larger than the compiler itself -- and is what carries `dtc`. `west sdk install` installs it by default (sdk.py:452: `if not args.interactive and not args.no_hosttools`). `--no-hosttools` nearly halves the on-disk store but loses `dtc`, which ties directly to ADR 0021's still-open dtc/gperf-on-Windows question. This file states the trade-off; it does not resolve it.

Scope honesty: the windows-x86_64 and macos-aarch64 artifact rows above are verified identity facts (URL, size, sha256) -- what those bundles CONTAIN (does the Windows minimal SDK ship `dtc`? `gperf` is confirmed absent) is still open per ADR 0021 and is deliberately not recorded or implied here.

tier/licence (issue #1603, follow-on to #1574): every row above is tier A per ADR 0021 SS3's own table (Zephyr SDK + arm-zephyr-eabi, hermetic archive, no elevation). licence is deliberately null on every row, not a guess: sdk-ng's own repo licence (Apache-2.0, its build scripts) is NOT what ships inside these archives -- upstream's .gitmodules (checked at the pinned v1.0.1 tag) shows both `minimal-sdk` (bundles openocd, qemu, bossa, gperf, dtc host tools) and `arm-zephyr-eabi-toolchain` (bundles binutils-gdb, gcc, picolibc) as multi-project, multi-licence composites -- the same shape issue #1574 already left `xz`/`7zip` null for in metadata/bootstrap.json's artifactProvenance, and a single SPDX id here would be exactly the fabricated-licence-on-a-consent-screen issue #1603 was opened to avoid.
